summary: @whalent/agent-core ships a fully obfuscated remote-agent daemon with PTY/SSH/RDP/VNC and self-replacement channel
details: The package's only shipped artifact is a 13.6 MB CommonJS bundle (dist/index.cjs), listed as both `main` and `bin`, wrapped with obfuscator.io transforms: a ~105k-entry rotating string array, control-flow flattening, and hex-name identifier renaming across ~400k nodes. All string literals, module paths, and API names are reconstructed at runtime, so the daemon's network destinations, shell dataflow, and update-fetch source cannot be audited from the shipped source. The bundle declares `node-pty` (PTY spawning), `ssh2` (SSH client/server), and WebSocket transports, and contains loopback references to `127.0.0.1:3389` (RDP), `127.0.0.1:5900` and `127.0.0.1:5901` (VNC), plus `process.env.SHELL` — the structural profile of a network-driven remote-shell / remote-desktop agent proxying a local shell or RDP/VNC session to a network peer. The README states the package is `replaced by remote daemon upgrades`, i.e. the code executing on the installer's host after initial install is whatever the upstream daemon pushes, through a channel that is itself obfuscated and cannot be verified for pinning, signature checks, or source. The combination — obfuscated bundle + advertised remote self-replacement + PTY/SSH/RDP/VNC surface — is a persistent remote-access channel into the installer's host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
